BURSEVI:v10p404/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p404/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p404/r1.claim: The ostentatious person displays extra humility and signs of piety so onlookers will think him righteous; riya is seeking worldly benefit through worship, unlike hypocrisy, which conceals disbelief beneath visible faith.
BURSEVI:v10p404/r1.anchor: والفرق بين المرائي والمنافق إن المنافق يبطن الكفر ويظهر الإيمان والمرائي يظهر زيادة الخشوع

BURSEVI:v10p404/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p404/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p404/r2.claim: In the inward reading, one who attributes deeds and states to the dark ego is an ostentatious person.
BURSEVI:v10p404/r2.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن من يضيف أعماله وأحواله إلى نفسه الظلمانية فهو مراىء

BURSEVI:v10p404/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p404/r5.speaker: برهان القرآن
BURSEVI:v10p404/r5.claim: Burhan al-Qur’an explains the repeated “those who are” as a grammatical necessity: the verse does not coordinate a verb directly with a noun, while repeating the phrase allows a verb to follow a verb.
BURSEVI:v10p404/r5.anchor: كرر ولم يقتصر على مرة واحدة لامتناع عطف الفعل على الاسم

QASHANI:107:7/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:107:7/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:107:7/r3.claim: They perform for show because they are veiled by creatures from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r5.claim: Because they are misers, the custodians will not spend for God's sake or even lend small items of common use.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r5.anchor: will never have the heart to even lend small items of gener al use

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r5.claim: The two closing verses identify ostentation and miserliness as the causes of impure, devotionless prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r5.anchor: they assert two reasons behind the lack of purity and devotion in their prayers: pretentiousness and miserliness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r6.claim: Sincere intention is prayer's essence: it should seek God's pleasure, while any other motive defeats its purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r6.anchor: Sincerity of intention is the essence of the prayer: it shoul d be offered just to please the Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r7.claim: The custodians pray to impress people, making their prayer a theatrical enactment rather than true worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r7.anchor: such a prayer is nothing more than a theatrical enactment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r1.claim: Prayer is the foremost expression of gratitude and leads a person to spend for God's sake; prayer and spending are the two pillars of the sharī‘ah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r1.anchor: the prayer is the foremost manifestation of the feeling of gratitude, and such a prayer subsequently motivates a person to spend on the needy

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r5.claim: Mean people pray to impress others, without inner motivation or effect on their hearts; ostentation increases their callousness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r5.anchor: they do only to impress others because they have no inner motivation for it

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says hypocrites leave prayer in private, perform it publicly, and rise lazily; the following mention of ostentation supports this reading, also attributed by Ibn Wahb to Mālik.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المنافقون يتركون الصلاة سرا ويفعلونها علانية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers an alternative syntax joining fa-dhālika to the one who denies judgment, omitting the answer to araʾayta, and making the woe to praying hypocrites a description standing for their pronoun; generic singular carries a plural sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.anchor: وطريقة أخرى أن يكون فذلك عطفا على الذي يكذب، إما عطف ذات على ذات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r5.claim: He notes that ostentation was discussed earlier in the commentary on al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r5.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الرياء في سورة البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r6.claim: The majority read yurāʾūn as the present tense of rāʾā, on the fāʿala pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يراءون مضارع راأى، على وزن فاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r7.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق والأشهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r7.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Ashhab read the form with hamza, a shortened vowel, and a doubled hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r7.anchor: وابن أبي إسحاق والأشهب: مهموزة مقصورة مشددة الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r8.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r8.claim: A further reading transmitted from Ibn Abī Isḥāq has no doubling of the hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r8.anchor: وعن ابن أبي إسحاق: بغير شد في الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r9.claim: He explains the first variant as making the hamza intensive to render the verb transitive, by analogy with deriving arā from raʾā and then rāʾā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r9.anchor: فتوجيه الأولى إلى أنه ضعف الهمزة تعدية، كما عدوا بالهمزة فقالوا في رأى: أرى، فقالوا: راأى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r10.claim: On this analysis, its imperfect and plural forms follow the pattern of yuṣallī and yuṣallūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r10.anchor: فجاء المضارع بأرى كيصلي، وجاء الجمع يروون كيصلون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r11.claim: He explains the second reading as easing the difficulty of doubling a hamza by making it lighter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r11.anchor: وتوجيه الثانية أنه استثقل التضعيف في الهمزة فخففها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r12.claim: Alternatively, the second reading may delete the alif from yurāʾūn without a motivating cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r12.anchor: أو حذف الألف من يراءون حذفا لا لسبب

FARRA:v3p294#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p294#2/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p294#2/r5.claim: They pray when people see them and leave prayer when nobody sees them.
FARRA:v3p294#2/r5.anchor: إن أبصرهم الناس صلوا، وإن لم يرهم أحد تركوا الصلاة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r1.claim: The description of showing off among hypocrites is linked to 4:142, where they rise for prayer lazily and for display.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r1.anchor: وقال في وصف المنافقين: "وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r2.claim: Qatada says they neglect prayer and do not care whether they pray.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: ساه عنها لا يبالي صلى أم لم يصل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r3.claim: Another view says they neither hope for reward when praying nor fear punishment when abandoning prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r3.anchor: وقيل: لا يرجون لها ثوابا إن صلوا ولا يخافون عقابا إن تركوا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r4.claim: Mujahid says they are heedless of prayer and treat it lightly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: غافلون عنها يتهاونون بها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r5.claim: Hasan says they pray only to be seen, and do not regret missing the prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الذي إن صلاها صلاها رياء، وإن فاتته لم يندم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says they fail to pray at the proper times and do not complete bowing and prostration.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p552/r6.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: لا يصلونها لمواقيتها ولا يتمون ركوعها وسجودها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r1.claim: Those who ostentatiously display their deeds do so so that people will praise them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r1.anchor: يرون الناس أعمالهم ليروهم الثناء عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.claim: The fa in the woe passage is consequential: neglect of the orphan already shows weak religion and deserves blame, so heedlessness of prayer, ostentation, and withholding zakāt merit it even more; prayer is religion's pillar, ostentation a branch of unbelief, and zakāt Islam's bridge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.anchor: فالسهو عن الصلاة التي هي عماد الدين والرياء الذي هو شعبة من الكفر، ومنع الزكاة التي هي قنطرة الإسلام أحق بذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.claim: Calling them “those who pray” in place of a pronoun signals their bad treatment of both the Creator and other people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.anchor: وإنما وضع المصلين موضع الضمير للدلالة على سوء معاملتهم مع الخالق والخلق

BINTSHATI:v2p189/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p189/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p189/r5.claim: The author treats the next clauses as attached to the inattentive worshippers: riya is showing people an outward state unlike one's inward one, near hypocrisy but also used more broadly.
BINTSHATI:v2p189/r5.anchor: ولا نفهم الآبة بمعزل عن الآية التالية لها وقد ارتبطت بها ارتباط الصلة بالموصول:

BINTSHATI:v2p189/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p189/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p189/r6.claim: The Quran uses riya for public display of giving or worship while faith or inner motives differ, across five passages.
BINTSHATI:v2p189/r6.anchor: وهو ما يؤنس إليه استعمال القرآن الكريم للرياء والمراءاة في الآيات الخمس

BINTSHATI:v2p191/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r1.claim: Some commentators limit condemned riya to optional worship, exempting required public duties and acts shown as examples for others.
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r1.anchor: وقد احترز عدد من المفسرين في تأويل: {يراءون (6) ويمنعون الماعون} من أن تتجه المراءاة إلى إظهار العمل الصالح

BINTSHATI:v2p191/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r2.claim: The author says this restriction is unnecessary: displaying obligatory worship or setting an example is not plausibly the condemned showing off.
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r2.anchor: وأرى السياق في غنى عن مثل هذا الاحتراز، إذ ليس في إظهار فرائض العبادات، ولا في موضع القدوة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.claim: He notes that people affiliated with Islam may push an orphan from his rights or fail to care for him, discourage feeding the poor, neglect prayer, show off, and withhold zakat or necessities.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.anchor: كدع اليتيم , وهو دفعه عن حقه وعدم الرفق به , وعدم الحض على طعام المسكين , والتغافل عن الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.claim: He reads these traits as those of a denier who expects no judgment, while observing that such acts can occur among Muslims without every person who commits them necessarily being a denier.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.anchor: فأخبر سبحانه وتعالى أنه من صفات من يكذب بيوم الدين ولا ينتظر الجزاء والحساب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r9.claim: The author compares this trait-based description to hadiths that call one with four specified traits a pure hypocrite and say a fornicator is not a believer while committing the act.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r1.claim: These people may do lesser good ostentatiously but are so dominated by greed that they cannot even show off by giving a trivial benefit; the best people in God's sight benefit His dependents most.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r1.anchor: إشعارا بأن أحب الخلق إلى الله أنفعهم لعياله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.claim: Al-Anfal 8:4 describes true believers as those who establish prayer and spend from God's provision, connecting with al-Ma'un's themes of prayer and giving.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.anchor: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r2.claim: The surah has twenty-five words; counting from the beginning of prophethood points to year twelve AH, when Abu Bakr had eliminated the apostates and zakat-refusers, exposing their earlier prayer and almsgiving as mere show.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r2.anchor: وذلك أن عدة كلماته خمس وعشرون كلمة فإذا اعتبرتها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r3.claim: Abu Bakr's campaigns ended in that year with the defeat of Banu Hanifa at Yamama, people of al-Nujayr in Kindah, and al-Aswad al-Ansi in Sanaa.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r3.anchor: ولم تمض تلك السنة إلا وقد فرغ منهم بالفراغ من بني حنيفة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r4.claim: The twenty-five words plus the four-word basmala point to year sixteen AH: Arab polytheists, Christians, and Magians had left the peninsula, most converting and the rest going to Byzantine lands.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r4.anchor: وما مضت سنة ست عشرة الموازية لعدد الكلمات بالبسملة - وذلك في أوائل خلافة الفاروق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r5.claim: The woe fell on showy worshippers who had been invited by their Prophet to pray but turned away, while other people followed them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r5.anchor: فحل الويل بالمرائين من أهل الصلاة فإنهم الذين أتى إليهم نبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصلاة فأعرضوا عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r6.claim: Counting pronouns is unsuitable because the religion had become openly manifest and unobstructed; counting letters is also unnecessary after its public triumph became clear.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r6.anchor: ولم يصح في هذه السورة اعتبار الضمائر لأن الدين في هذا الحد كان قد ظهر على كل ظاهر

NAHHAS:v5p297/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p297/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p297/r1.claim: The hypocrites do not pray from fear of punishment or hope of reward; they pray only to be seen by Muslims and avoid bloodshed.
NAHHAS:v5p297/r1.anchor: أي لا يصلون خوفا من عقاب ولا رجاء لثواب ولكن لينظرهم المسلمون فلا يسفكون دماءهم وهم المنافقون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r1.claim: Fronting “they” before the predicate strengthens the judgment that they perform prayer for show.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r1.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على الخبر الفعلي في قوله : { هم يراءون } لتقوية الحكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r2.claim: If the surah or its final three verses are Medinan, “those who pray” means hypocrites who only appear to pray; the verb names the appearance of the act, as “the hypocrites fear” means they seem to fear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r2.anchor: فأما على القول بأن السورة مدنية أو بأن هذه الآيات الثلاث مدنية يكون المراد بالمصلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r4.claim: The causal fa makes the show-praying hypocrites part of the deniers of Judgment who mistreat orphans and fail to urge feeding the poor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r4.anchor: فلما عرفوا بهذه الخلال كان مفاد فاء التفريع أن أولئك المتظاهرين بالصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r5.speaker: هبة الله بن سلامة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r5.claim: Hibat Allah ibn Salama says the final three verses were revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubay ibn Salul, with a plural expression for one person as in the people of Noah denying the messengers, meaning their messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r5.anchor: وحكى هبة الله بن سلامة في كتاب ( الناسخ والمنسوخ ) : أن هذه الآيات الثلاث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r6.claim: Sahw literally means inadvertent forgetfulness, but here it sarcastically means deliberate neglect; genuine forgetfulness in prayer is not the target because it is excused for this community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r6.anchor: والسهو حقيقته : الذهول عن أمر سبق علمه ، وهو هنا مستعار للإعراض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r7.claim: The deliberate-neglect sense parallels “forgetting” one's associates as turning away, and being heedless of signs in al-Aʿraf and Yunus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r7.anchor: ومثله استعارة الغفلة للإعراض في قوله تعالى : { بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r8.claim: When a later revelation is attached to an earlier one, God shapes its wording to fit the connection; the consequential fa is a clue worth watching in such cases.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r8.anchor: واعلم أنه إذا أراد الله إنزال شيء من القرآن ملحقا بشيء قبله جعل نظم الملحق مناسبا لما هو متصل به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r14.claim: Their prayer is performed for people rather than God and therefore is not an evident act of faith acceptable to Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r14.anchor: وقوله تعالى: الذين هم يراؤن بيان أن صلاة هؤلاء ليست لله تعالى بينة إيمان، وإنما هي رياء للبشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r15.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وأبو الأشهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r15.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu al-Ashhab read yuraʾun with an emphasized hamza; another report from Ibn Abi Ishaq omits the emphasis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق وأبو الأشهب: «يرؤون» مهموزة مقصورة مشددة الهمزة،

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، عكرمة، قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Ikrima, and Qatada classify the seven-verse sura as Meccan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.anchor: قيل: مكية، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.speaker: الضحاك، الواقدي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Waqidi classify the sura as Medinan.

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.claim: Muqatil says it is Meccan through the mention of the needy, with the remainder Medinan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.anchor: مكية إلى قوله: (المسكين) وباقي السورة مدنية، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.claim: A report transmitted from Ubayy says reciting this sura brings God's forgiveness for one who pays zakat; no grading is given.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (أرأيت) غفر الله له

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.claim: After recounting favors to Quraysh, the sura marvels at their conduct despite Meccan security and provision, then their denial of the Prophet and his prophethood.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.anchor: افتتح هذه السورة تعجبا من حالهم مع عظم النعم عليهم بمكة من الأمن والرزق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r4.claim: Mura'ah is a reciprocal display: the person shows people his deed, and they return praise and admiration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r4.anchor: هي مفاعلة من الإراءة ، لأن المرائي يرى الناس عمله ، وهم يرونه الثناء عليه والإعجاب به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r5.claim: Displaying obligatory acts is not ostentation: they should be public as religious signs, and doing so removes suspicion and blame for neglect.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r5.anchor: فمن حق الفرائض الإعلان بها وتشهيرها ، لقوله عليه الصلاة السلام : ( 1346 ) ( ولا غمة في فرائض الله ) لأنها أعلام الإسلام وشعائر الدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r6.claim: Voluntary acts should normally be concealed because leaving them incurs no blame or suspicion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r6.anchor: وإن كان تطوعا ، فحقه أن يخفي ، لأنه مما لا يلام برتكه ولا تهمة فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r7.claim: Showing a voluntary act is good when intended as an example, but it is ostentation when done to win praise for piety.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r7.anchor: فإن أظهره قاصدا للاقتداء به كان جميلا ، وإنما الرياء أن يقصد بالإظهار أن تراه الأعين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r8.speaker: بعضهم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r8.claim: An unnamed observer suspected ostentation when a man prolonged a thanksgiving prostration in the mosque and remarked it would be better at home.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r8.anchor: وعن بعضهم : أنه رأى رجلا في المسجد قد سجد سجدة الشكر وأطالها ، فقال : ما أحسن هذا لو كان في بيتك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r9.claim: Avoiding ostentation is difficult except for those disciplined in sincerity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r9.anchor: على أن اجتناب الرياء صعب إلا على المرتاضين بالإخلاص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r10.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r10.claim: The Prophet says ostentation is subtler than a black ant crawling on a black surface in a dark night.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p809/r10.anchor: ومن ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1347 ) ( الرياء أخفى من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة المظلمة على المسح الأسود )

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r23.speaker: علي، ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r23.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas say those who display their deeds are hypocrites who pray when people are present and not when absent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r23.anchor: المنافقون الذين يراءون بصلاتهم , يصلونها مع الناس إذا حضروا , ولا يصلونها إذا غابوا , قاله علي وابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r24.claim: The verse can broadly condemn anyone who performs a deed for show without seeking God's sincere favor; a report from the Prophet says God rejects work done for another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r24.anchor: عام في ذم كل من راءى لعمله ولم يقصد به إخلاصا لوجه ربه

MUQATIL:107:1-7/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r7.claim: They perform prayer to be seen by people and do not intend it for God.
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r7.anchor: إذا أبصرهم الناس صلوا، يراءون الناس بذلك، ولا يريدون الله عز وجل بها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r5.claim: Riyāʾ is reciprocal display: the show-off presents deeds to people, seeking their praise and admiration.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r5.anchor: والمرا آة مفاعلة من الاراءة لأن المرائى يرائى الناس عمله وهم يرونه الثناء عليه والإعجاب به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r6.claim: Public performance of obligatory duties is not ostentation because they are meant to be public; voluntary worship is better hidden, though showing it to encourage imitation is good.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#4/r6.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائيا باظهار الفرائض فمن حقها الاعلان بها لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا عمة فى فرائض الله والاخفاء فى التطوع أولى

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Māʿūn an early Makkan sūrah after al-Takāthur, though some assign vv. 4–7 to Madinah; since the whole sūrah addresses religious hypocrisy, it may all be Madinan, when hypocrisy could gain political advantage.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.anchor: commentators maintain that al-Māʿūn is an early Makkan sūrah

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.claim: Religious hypocrisy is not treated as limited to Muslims alone.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.anchor: Nonetheless, hypocrisy in religion was not seen as limited to Muslims alone.

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed in the mission's early years, probably after surah 102; its title comes from al-ma'un in the last verse.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.anchor: revealed in the early years of the Prophet's mission (probably after surah 102), is derived from the word al-ma'un occurring in the last verse

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.speaker: some commentators
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.claim: Some commentators date verses 4–7 to Medina, but Asad rejects this view for lack of historical or textual evidence.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.anchor: The view of some commentators that verses 4-7 were revealed at Medina lacks all historical or textual evidence and may, therefore, be disregarded.

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Rudolph
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:anmerkung/r1.claim: Rudolph compares the sura's polemic against ostentatious prayer with Matthew 6:5, where hypocrites pray publicly to be seen by people.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Gegen eine äußerliche Verrichtung des Gebets polemisiert schon Matthäus 6:5

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.claim: The second section opens with the emphatic wail that introduces a catalogue of vices.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.anchor: einen rhetorisch markanten Einsatzpunkt auf, nämlich die einen Lasterkatalog einleitende Interjektion „Wehe …“ (wail)

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.claim: Verses 4–6 target the criticized people's neglect of ritual prayer.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die anschließenden Verse zielen zunächst (V. 4–6) auf die kultische Nachlässigkeit der Getadelten ab

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.claim: The two groups cross-correspond: verse 1 and verses 4–6 concern religious omissions, while verses 2–3 and verse 7 concern social omissions; the first group stresses social failings and the second religious ones.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.anchor: Inhaltlich korrespondieren insofern V. 1 und V. 4–6 (religiöse Unterlassungen) und V. 2.3 und V. 7 (soziale Unterlassungen)

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.claim: The surah warns people professing religion whose traits resemble hypocrites: neglecting prayer, acting ostentatiously, and withholding aid, all incompatible with belief in requital.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.anchor: بيان وعيد لمن كان من المنتحلين بالدين متخلقا بأخلاق المنافقين

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.claim: The surah may be Meccan or Medinan; another view says its first half is Meccan and second half Medinan.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية، وقيل نصفها مكي ونصفها مدني

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r12.claim: They perform worship to be seen by people, working for them rather than for God.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r12.anchor: أي يأتون بالعبادات لمرآة الناس فهم يعملون للناس لا لله تعالى

TABATABAI:107:5-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r3.claim: A report from Ali explains those who show off as people who display their prayers.
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب { الذين هم يراءون } قال يراؤن بصلاتهم

TABRISI:107:5-7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:107:5-7/r1.speaker: علي، ابن عباس
TABRISI:107:5-7/r1.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas are cited for the view that these are hypocrites who delay prayer until its time passes, then pray for show among believers and omit it when alone, expecting no reward and fearing no penalty.
TABRISI:107:5-7/r1.anchor: فإذا كانوا مع المؤمنين صلوها رياء وإذا لم يكونوا معهم لم يصلوا وهو قوله { الذين هم يراؤون } عن علي ع وابن عباس

TABRISI:107:5-7/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:107:5-7/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:107:5-7/r11.claim: One view says they perform all their deeds for people and intend no sincerity toward God.
TABRISI:107:5-7/r11.anchor: في جميع أعمالهم لم يقصدوا بها الإخلاص لله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the hypocrites leave prayer in private and perform it in public.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يتركون الصلاة في السر، ويصلونها في العلانية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says they pray when someone sees them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r2.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الكلبي: إن أبصرهم أحد صلوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r3.claim: The quoted description of them as showing off to people means they do not intend their prayer for God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r3.anchor: كقوله: (يراؤون الناس) أي لا يريدون الله بها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r4.claim: Show-offs are hypocrites who pray publicly and abandon prayer in private.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r4.anchor: { الذين هم يراؤون } يعني: المنافقين يصلون في العلانية، ويتركون الصلاة في السر.

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r16.claim: The hypocrites perform deeds for public display and people's approval rather than for God.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r16.anchor: Her ne amel yapsalar Allah için yapmazlar da halka gösteriş için ve herkesin göreceği yerde yaparlar

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.claim: Religious pretenders who neglect prayer, show off, and withhold even small help are more astonishingly blameworthy than disbelievers who deny religion and mistreat orphans and the poor.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.anchor: namaz kılar dindar görünüp de namazlarından yanılan, mürâîlik, gösteriş yapıp

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.claim: After the address to the Prophet to see and understand, Sūrat al-Kawthar condenses the preceding suras, especially those from al-Ḍuḥā, as a final account of Muhammad's rank.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.anchor: Ve’d-Duhâ’dan beri gelen sûrelerin mazmûnu üzerinde hepsinin tetimmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r5.claim: Riya is presenting a religious or moral virtue one lacks and pursuing material or spiritual gain through apparent goodness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r5.anchor: bir kimsenin, kendisinde bulunmayan dinî ve ahlâkî bir meziyeti, bir erdemi varmış gibi göstermesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.claim: Outward forms of worship remain essential, but equal care is due to its inner substance: faith, intention, sincerity, reverence, and piety.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.anchor: şekil şartları da vazgeçilmez olmakla birlikte, en az şekil kadar özen gösterilmesi gereken husus

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.claim: Intention and sincerity in worship reflect the principle of divine unity, as illustrated by the cited verses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.anchor: Kur’an’a göre ibadetlerde niyet ve ihlâs, tevhid ilkesinin ibadetteki yansımasıdır

BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r12.claim: The show-offs want people to see their worship so they will praise them; using seeing for praise is a general figurative expression or means recognition.
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r12.anchor: أي يرون الناس مالهم ليروهم الثناء عليها

BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r13.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r13.claim: Al-Kashshāf says obligatory worship should be public to remove suspicion because it is an emblem of Islam, while voluntary worship is usually better hidden.
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r13.anchor: قال في "الكشاف" والعمل الصالح إن كان فريضة فمن حق الفرائض

BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r14.claim: Showing a voluntary act to encourage imitation is good; ostentation is acting so that eyes will see and praise, and avoiding it is exceptionally difficult.
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r14.anchor: وإن أظهره قاصدا للاقتداء فيه كان جميلا وإنما الرياء أن يقصد أن تراه الأعين فتثنى عليه بالصلاح

SULAMI:v2p421#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p421#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p421#2/r1.claim: Show-offs lack sincere deeds, do not require sincerity of themselves, and pursue their standing and appearance before people rather than an inspiration that turns them from human notice.
SULAMI:v2p421#2/r1.anchor: قال الذين هم لا يخلصون لله عملا ، ولا يطالبون أنفسهم بحقيقة الإخلاص

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r1.claim: Ali says those who show off are people who display their prayer for others.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله : الذين هم يراءون قال يراءون بصلاتهم

TUSTARI:107:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:107:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:107:6/r1.claim: Showing off is hidden shirk: hypocrites pray well in mosques but become lax when Muslims cannot see them, as the warning that follows calling them worshippers demonstrates.
TUSTARI:107:6/r1.anchor: قال: هو الشرك الخفي، لأن المنافقين كانوا يحسنون الصلاة في المساجد، فإذا غابوا عن أعين المسلمين تكاسلوا عنها،

TUSTARI:107:6/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:107:6/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:107:6/r2.claim: Shirk is either in God's essence, which is unforgivable, or in one's conduct, such as worshiping so people praise one's pilgrimage and prayer.
TUSTARI:107:6/r2.anchor: واعلموا أن الشرك شركان: شرك في ذات الله عز وجل، وشرك في معاملته،

TUSTARI:107:6/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:107:6/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:107:6/r3.claim: A report commands sincere acts because God accepts only what is pure for Him, and rejects dividing an act between God and kinship.
TUSTARI:107:6/r3.anchor: وفي الخبر: أخلصوا أعمالكم لله فإن الله لا يقبل من العمل إلا ما خلص،

TUSTARI:107:6/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:107:6/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:107:6/r4.claim: The Prophet tells Muadh that sincerity toward God makes a small amount of work sufficient.
TUSTARI:107:6/r4.anchor:
وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ حين قال له: أوصني يا رسول الله، قال:
" أخلص لله يكفيك القليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r10.claim: The example is the late Asr prayer, performed without calm or reverence and perhaps only for show, like the hypocrites described elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r10.anchor: ولعله إنما حمله على القيام إليها مراءاة الناس،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r1.claim: A report describes a valley in Hell that Hell itself seeks refuge from four hundred times daily, prepared for ostentatious people including a Qur'an-bearer, almsgiver, pilgrim, and fighter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r1.anchor: أعد ذلك الوادي للمرائين من أمة محمد: لحامل كتاب الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r2.claim: Whoever publicizes his deed so people will hear of it will have God expose and disgrace him before creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r2.anchor: من سمع الناس بعمله، سمع الله به سامع خلقه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r3.claim: Doing a deed for God and then feeling pleased when people see it does not count as ostentation, as a report promises reward for both secrecy and publicity.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r4.claim: In a report Ibn Kathir calls strange through this chain, a man pleased that someone saw his prayer is told he has two rewards, for private and public worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r4.anchor: كتب لك أجران: أجر السر، وأجر العلانية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r5.speaker: ابن المبارك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak is quoted as calling the report a good hadith for people who ostentatiously perform deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verses describe hypocrites who leave prayer privately but perform it publicly, matching 4:142; Malik reports the same interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة سرا

QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r11.claim: Showing worship to people while claiming devotion is ostentation; its true aim is worldly gain and status in people’s hearts.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r11.anchor: وحقيقة الرياء طلب ما في الدنيا بالعبادة، وأصله طلب المنزلة في قلوب الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r12.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r12.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi lists ostentation through appearance, coarse clothing, public speech, and displaying or beautifying prayer and charity to be seen.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r12.anchor: وأولها تحسين السمت وهو من أجزاء النبوة، ويريد بذلك الجاه والثناء

QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r13.claim: Publicly displaying a required good deed is not ostentation, because obligatory acts properly may be announced and made visible.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:4-6/r13.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائيا بإظهار العمل الصالح إن كان فريضة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.claim: Although Qutb leans toward a wholly Medinan setting because hypocrisy and ostentation were unfamiliar in Mecca, he allows later verses to have been appended for thematic continuity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.anchor: وإن كانت السورة كلها وحدة متماسكة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.claim: The seven short verses overturn conventional ideas of faith and disbelief and reveal the creed’s mercy and immense good for humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة الصغيرة ذات الآيات السبع القصيرة تعالج حقيقة ضخمة تكاد تبدل المفهوم السائد للإيمان والكفر

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.claim: Religion is an integrated way of life whose worship, rites, and personal and social duties purify hearts and lead people to cooperation, care, and flourishing.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.anchor: إنما هو منهج متكامل ، تتعاون عباداته وشعائره

QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.claim: Those heedless worshippers are the ones who show off and withhold small acts of help.

QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r1.claim: They pray for people’s approval instead of sincerely for God, so they remain heedless of the prayer they are performing.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r1.anchor: إنهم يصلون رياء للناس لا إخلاصا لله

QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r2.claim: The required act is establishing prayer, which requires conscious presence and standing before God alone.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r2.anchor: وإقامتها لا تكون إلا باستحضار حقيقتها

RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r1.claim: The threat covers three sins: heedlessness about prayer, ostentation, and withholding small aid; since these do not alone make a Muslim hypocrite, commentators explain why the warning is so severe.

RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r1.claim: A hypocrite displays faith while concealing unbelief; a show-off displays extra humility absent from the heart to seem devout, or differs from a hypocrite because his public prayer is better than his private prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r1.anchor: أن المنافق هو المظهر للإيمان المبطن للكفر ، والمرائي المظهر

RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r2.claim: Obligatory prayers and alms should be public as Islamic emblems to prevent suspicion; voluntary worship is usually concealed unless shown to encourage imitation.
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r2.anchor: يجب إظهار الفرائض من الصلاة والزكاة لأنها شعائر الإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r3.claim: Someone saw a man prolonging prostration of thanks in a mosque and remarked that it would be admirable if done at home.
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r3.anchor: في المسجد رجلا يسجد للشكر وأطالها

RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r4.claim: One should neither abandon voluntary worship from embarrassment nor perform it for show; ostentation is difficult to avoid.
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r4.anchor: لا يترك النوافل حياء ولا يأتى بها رياء

RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r5.claim: The Prophet compares ostentation’s subtlety to a black ant moving in a dark night over a black stone.
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r5.anchor: الرياء أخفى من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة الظلماء على المسح الأسود

RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r6.claim: Riya is a reciprocal form of showing: the ostentatious person displays deeds, while observers return praise and admiration.
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r6.anchor: هي مفاعلة من الإرادة لأن المرائي يرى الناس عمله

RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r7.claim: Heedlessness from prayer indicates both praying outside its time and being distracted within it; with ostentation added, prayer must be free from all three conditions.
RAZI-FULL:v32p107#3/r7.anchor: إخراجها عن الوقت ، وكون الإنسان غافلا فيها

STUDYQURAN:107:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r1.claim: Those who seek to be seen are hypocrites, like people who pray idly for human attention and remember God little.
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r1.anchor: Those who strive to be seen are the hypocrites, of whom the Quran says, When they perform the prayer

STUDYQURAN:107:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r2.claim: Their prayer serves reputation rather than worship.
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r2.anchor: they do not perform prayer out of worship, but only to increase their reputation

STUDYQURAN:107:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r3.claim: They contrast with those who are constant in prayer and those mindful of their prayers.
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r3.anchor: as opposed to those who are constant in their prayers (70:23) and those who are mindful of their prayers (70:34)

STUDYQURAN:107:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r4.claim: The Qur'an's treatment of hypocrisy and dissimilitude is discussed at 63:1–8.
STUDYQURAN:107:6/r4.anchor: For the Quranic treatment of hypocrisy and dissimilitude, see 63:1–8.

TAB:107:4/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:4/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are hypocrites who display prayer before people, abandon it when unseen, and withhold borrowed household goods.
TAB:107:4/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : { فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون } فهم المنافقون كانوا يراؤون الناس بصلاتهم إذا حضروا

TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r1.claim: The hypocrites hid disbelief and displayed Islam, which let believers treat them as Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r1.anchor: يستبطنون الكفر، ويظهرون الإسلام، كذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r3.claim: ʿAlī says they show off through their prayers.
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، عليه السلام في قوله: يراءون ويمنعون الماعون قال: «يراءون بصلاتهم»

TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies those heedless and ostentatious as hypocrites.
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون} «يعني المنافقين»

TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says hypocrites pray ostentatiously in public and stop praying when unseen.
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «هم المنافقون؛ كانوا يراءون الناس بصلاتهم إذا حضروا، ويتركونها إذا غابوا»

TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says they perform prayers as ostentation, though prayer is not their true practice.
TAB-FULL:v24p664#2/r6.anchor: ثني ابن زيد: «ويصلون، وليس الصلاة من شأنهم رياء»

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains that the hypocrite withholds zakāt, prays for display, and feels no regret if he misses prayer.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.anchor: عن الحسن، " {الذين هم يراءون ويمنعون الماعون}

WAHIDI-QT:107:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:107:6/r1.claim: Hypocrites pray publicly but abandon prayer in private.
WAHIDI-QT:107:6/r1.anchor: { الذين هم يراؤون } يعني المنافقين يصلون في العلانية ،   ويتركون الصلاة في السر

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r1.claim: Damascus, Mecca, and Medina verse counts do not end a verse after yurāʾūn; Neuwirth considers this formally plausible because 83:1–3 similarly has a short woe introduction followed by two longer vice-catalogue verses.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r1.anchor: formkritisch ist dies deshalb plausibel, weil auch in dem Wehspruch 83:1–3 auf einen kürzeren Einleitungsvers

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.claim: If verses 6–7 are combined despite the rhyme potential at yurāʾūn, the sura has a symmetrical structure of two triads.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.anchor: so ergibt sich für Sure 107 ein symmetrischer Aufbau von zwei Dreiergruppen

ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#4/r1.claim: They perform prayer when people can see them, seeking praise.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#4/r1.anchor: الناس فيعلمون حيث يروا الناس ويرونهم طلبا للثناء عليهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they are hypocrites who omit prayer when unobserved but pray publicly when people are present, as in the description of those who show off.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة إذا غابوا عن الناس، ويصلونها في العلانية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.claim: Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.anchor: مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث ، فإنه يجزئ المكذب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.claim: Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostentation and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.anchor: إن هذه كلها من شأن المكذب بالحساب والجزاء لأن نفع البعد عنها إنما يكون إذ ذاك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r10.claim: Their neglect means abandoning prayer privately and corrupting its inward quality in public; ostentation makes them perform deeds to win praise or kindness, not hope for reward or fear of God's punishment, so they leave prayer when unseen.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r10.anchor: تضييعها عند الانفراد بالترك حسا ومعنى وعند الاجتماع بالإفساد في المعنى : { الذين هم }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.claim: The commands answer al-Māʿūn's four vices: giving counters stinginess, prayer counters neglect, exclusive devotion counters ostentation, and sacrifice counters withholding alms.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.anchor: وقد قابل في هذا أربعا من سورة الدين بأربع , وهي البخل بالإعطاء , وإضاعة الصلاة بالأمر بها

DURR:107:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:6/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:107:6/r1.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says they show off through their prayers.
DURR:107:6/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب { الذين هم يراؤون } قال : يراؤون بصلاتهم

DURR-FULL:v8p642/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p642/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p642/r11.claim: Ali explains the following description, “those who show off,” as showing off through their prayers.
DURR-FULL:v8p642/r11.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب {الذين هم يراؤون} قال: يراؤون بصلاتهم

TAB:107:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:107:6/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains that hypocrites display their prayers so believers will think them Muslim and refrain from killing them or capturing their families; they seek neither reward nor fear of punishment, concealing disbelief while showing Islam.
TAB:107:6/r1.anchor: يقول :  الذين هم يراؤون الناس بصلاتهم إذا صَلّوْا ؛  لأنهم لا يصلّون رغبةً في ثواب ،   ولا رهبةً من عقاب ،   وإنما يصلونها ليراهم المؤمنون فيظنونهم منهم

TAB:107:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:6/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB:107:6/r3.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib explains their ostentation as showing off through prayer.
TAB:107:6/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ،   عن مجاهد ،   عن عليّ بن أبي طالب عليه السلام في قوله :  {  يُرَاءُونَ وَيمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  يراؤون بصلاتهم .

TAB:107:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:6/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:107:6/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the heedless worshippers and those who show off are hypocrites.
TAB:107:6/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  {  الّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ ساهُونَ الّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ } يعني المنافقين .

TAB:107:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:6/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the hypocrites show their prayers when people are present and leave prayer when they are absent.
TAB:107:6/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  هم المنافقون ،   كانوا يراؤون الناس بصلاتهم إذا حضروا ،   ويتركونها إذا غابوا .

TAB:107:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:6/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:107:6/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says they perform prayer ostentatiously even though prayer is not part of their usual conduct.

BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman says Surat al-Maun is Meccan except from فويل للمصلين through its end, which is Medinan.
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.anchor: سورة ﴿ أرأيت ﴾ مكية إلا قوله ﴿ فويل للمصلين ﴾ إلى آخرها فإنها مدنية كذا قال مقاتل بن سليمان

ITQAN:v3p297/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.claim: Al-Kawthar counters al-Ma'un's four traits: abundant giving opposes miserliness, prayer opposes neglect, worship for God opposes showing off, and sacrifice meat is charity opposing withholding small kindnesses.
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.anchor: لأن السابقة وصف الله فيها المنافق بأربعة أمور البخل وترك الصلاة والرياء فيها ومنع الزكاة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.claim: The preposition عن makes the warning concern heedlessness of prayer's purpose: standing before God, restraining wrongdoing, cultivating humility, and prompting care for orphans and the poor.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.anchor: فنرى النذير بالويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون غافلون عن كونها قياما بين يدي الخالق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.claim: This is not forgetfulness during prayer, abandoning prayer or its time, or fidgeting and yawning; some pray on time and feign humility for an audience or benefit, turning prayer into ostentation and formal hypocrisy.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.anchor: ليس السهو عن الصلاة إذن سهوا فيها ولا تركا لها أو ترك وقتها

ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r1.claim: The discussion of showing off was already treated in Sūrat al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r1.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الرياء في سورة البقرة

ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r2.claim: The majority read yurāʾūna, the imperfect of rāʾā on the fāʿala pattern.
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : يراءون مضارع راأى ،   على وزن فاعل

ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق والأشهب
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Ashhab read with the hamza shortened and doubled.
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r3.anchor: وابن أبي إسحاق والأشهب : مهموزة مقصورة مشددة الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r4.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r4.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq is also reported reading without doubling the hamza.
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r4.anchor: وعن ابن أبي إسحاق : بغير شد في الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r5.claim: The first variant is explained as strengthening the hamza to make the verb transitive, by analogy with making raʾā transitive as arā; its imperfect is compared with yuṣallī.
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r5.anchor: فتوجيه الأولى إلى أنه ضعف الهمزة تعدية

ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r6.claim: The other variant is explained either as easing a heavy doubled hamza or as deleting the alif without a phonological cause.
ABUHAYYAN:107:6/r6.anchor: وتوجيه الثانية أن استثقل التضعيف في الهمزة فخففها ،   أو حذف الألف من يراءون حذفا لا لسبب

ALUSI:107:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:6/r1.claim: They act when people can see them and let themselves be seen, seeking praise.
ALUSI:107:6/r1.anchor: الناس فيعملون حيث يروا الناس ويرونهم طلباً للثناء عليهم

ALUSI:107:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r11.claim: The fāʾ in fa-wayl is consequential: the discourse escalates from orphan-pushing to prayer-neglect, ostentation, and withholding zakāt or customary loans, increasingly exposing denial of religion.
ALUSI:107:7/r11.anchor: جزائية والكلام ترق من ذلك المعرف إلى معرف أقوى

ALUSI:107:7/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r16.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI:107:7/r16.claim: The Kashf author says that if the orphan-pusher is a named individual, treating the later prayer-neglect and ostentation as further identifying labels is ill-fitting; those clauses work as a digression prompted by the orphan-pushing description.
ALUSI:107:7/r16.anchor: قال «صاحب الكشف » غير ملائم بل يكون شبه استطراد

ALUSI:107:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's main concern is denial of religion, using orphan-abuse as its identifying sign and the later vices to press the question whether such conduct is good or evil, like the rebuke in 5:91.
ALUSI:107:7/r17.anchor: فكأنه قيل أخبرني ما تقول فيمن يكذبون بالدين وفيمن يؤذون اليتيم

ALUSI:107:7/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r18.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:107:7/r18.claim: Some make the fāʾ causal from the preceding coordination, requiring the worshippers and deniers to be one group; they are then identified as hypocrites, a reading reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Mālik, and supported by the ostentation clause.
ALUSI:107:7/r18.anchor: وجعل بعضهم الفاء في فويل على العطف المذكور للسببية وهذا الوجه يقتضي اتحاد المصلين والمكذبين

ALUSI:107:7/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r19.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والإمام مالك
ALUSI:107:7/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Imām Mālik are reported to identify the worshippers as hypocrites; al-Baḥr cites the ostentation description as evidence.
ALUSI:107:7/r19.anchor: بل روى إطلاق القول بأنهم المرادون عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والإمام مالك

ALUSI:107:7/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r24.speaker: ابن إسحق والأشهب
ALUSI:107:7/r24.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and al-Ashhab read yarāʾūna with a shortened form and a doubled hamza.
ALUSI:107:7/r24.anchor: وقرأ ابن إسحق والأشهب يرؤون بالقصر وتشديد الهمزة

ALUSI:107:7/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r25.speaker: ابن إسحق
ALUSI:107:7/r25.claim: Another narration from Ibn Isḥāq gives the shortened reading without doubling the hamza.
ALUSI:107:7/r25.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن ابن إسحق أنه قرأ بالقصر وترك التشديد

BAGHAWI:107:4/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:107:4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are hypocrites who omit prayer when away from people but pray publicly when seen, as the next verse says they show off.
BAGHAWI:107:4/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة إذا غابوا عن الناس ، ويصلونها في العلانية إذا حضروا

BAGHAWI:107:5/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:107:5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are hypocrites who omit prayer when away from people but pray publicly when seen, as the next verse says they show off.
BAGHAWI:107:5/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة إذا غابوا عن الناس ، ويصلونها في العلانية إذا حضروا

BAGHAWI:107:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:107:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are hypocrites who omit prayer when away from people but pray publicly when seen, as the next verse says they show off.
BAGHAWI:107:6/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة إذا غابوا عن الناس ، ويصلونها في العلانية إذا حضروا

BAYDAWI:107:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:6/r1.claim: They display their deeds to people so that people will praise them.
BAYDAWI:107:6/r1.anchor: يرون الناس أعمالهم ليروهم الثناء عليهم

BAYDAWI:107:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:7/r3.claim: If disregard for the orphan shows weak religion, heedlessness of prayer, ostentation, and withholding zakāt deserve woe even more; prayer is religion’s pillar, ostentation a branch of unbelief, and zakāt its bridge.
BAYDAWI:107:7/r3.anchor: فالسهو عن الصلاة التي هي عماد الدين ، والرياء الذي هو شعبة من الكفر ، ومنع الزكاة التي هي قنطرة الإسلام ، أحق بذلك ، ولذلك رتب عليها الويل

BIQAI:107:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:6/r1.claim: Their heedlessness means abandoning prayer materially when alone and corrupting it inwardly when gathered with others.
BIQAI:107:6/r1.anchor: قال دالاًّ على أن المراد بالسهو ههنا تضييعها عند الانفراد بالترك حساً ومعنى ، وعند الاجتماع بالإفساد في المعنى

BIQAI:107:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:6/r2.claim: They display prayer and other good deeds so people will see them, praise them, and do them favors, rather than seeking reward or fearing God's punishment.
BIQAI:107:6/r2.anchor: أي بصلاتهم وغيرها يرون الناس أنهم يفعلون الخير ليراهم الناس

BIQAI:107:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:6/r3.claim: Because they seek only present people's approval, they leave prayer when no one is watching.
BIQAI:107:6/r3.anchor: لا لرجاء الثواب ، ولا لمخوف العقاب من الله سبحانه وتعالى ، ولذلك يتركون الصلاة إذا غابوا عن الناس

IBNASHUR:107:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:5/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:5/r5.claim: The author connects this insincere prayer to the hypocrites described as showing off and remembering God only a little.
IBNASHUR:107:5/r5.anchor: { يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلاً في المنافقين }

IBNASHUR:107:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:5/r6.claim: They intend people to see an apparently good state that is false, so people will praise qualities they do not possess.
IBNASHUR:107:5/r6.anchor: و ( يراءون ) يقصدون أن يرى الناس أنهم على حال حسن

IBNASHUR:107:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:5/r7.claim: The verb occurs in the reciprocal form; no simple form is attested, since the act entails repeated display.
IBNASHUR:107:5/r7.anchor: وارد في الكلام على صيغة المفاعلة ولم يسمع منه فعل مجرد

IBNASHUR:107:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:6/r1.claim: Putting the subject pronoun before the verbal predicate strengthens and emphasizes the assertion.
IBNASHUR:107:6/r1.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على الخبر الفعلي في قوله

IBNASHUR:107:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:6/r2.claim: On the Medinan view, these are hypocrites; calling them worshipers means they outwardly present themselves as praying, as in the verse about hypocrites appearing to fear a sura's revelation.
IBNASHUR:107:6/r2.anchor: فإطلاق المصلين عليهم بمعنى المتظاهرين بأنهم يصلون

IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.speaker: هبة الله بن سلامة
IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.claim: Hibat Allah ibn Salama reports in al-Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh that these three verses were revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.
IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.anchor: وحكى هبة الله بن سلامة في كتاب « الناسخ والمنسوخ »

IBNATIYYA:107:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r1.claim: Their prayer is not offered to God with faith, but is done to show off before people; therefore it is not accepted.
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { الذين هم يراؤون } بيان أن صلاة هؤلاء ليست لله تعالى بنية إيمان

IBNATIYYA:107:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r2.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وأبو الأشهب
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu al-Ashhab read the form with a shortened vowel and a doubled hamza.
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق وأبو الأشهب : «يرؤن » مهموزة مقصورة مشددة الهمزة

IBNATIYYA:107:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r3.claim: A second reading reported from Ibn Abi Ishaq has the hamza undoubled.
IBNATIYYA:107:6/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن أبي إسحاق : «يرؤون » بغير شد في الهمزة

IBNKATHIR:107:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet's account of a valley in Hell that Hell seeks refuge from 400 times daily, prepared for show-offs including Qur'an reciters, givers, pilgrims, and those who go out in God's path.
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR:107:6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r2.claim: The Prophet says that whoever publicizes deeds for people will have God publicize him among creation and humiliate him; Ahmad gives another route through an unnamed man.
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r2.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو يقول : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:107:6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r3.speaker: ابن المبارك
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak remarks, after the Abu Hurayra report about public notice, that it is a good hadith for show-offs.
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r3.anchor: بلغني أن ابن المبارك قال : نعم الحديث للمرائين

IBNKATHIR:107:6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r4.claim: An act done for God does not become ostentation merely because people see it and the doer feels pleased by that.
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r4.anchor: أن من عمل عملا لله فاطلع عليه الناس ، فأعجبه ذلك ، أن هذا لا يعد رياء

IBNKATHIR:107:6/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet promised two rewards, for secret and public worship, when a man who had prayed privately was pleased that a visitor saw him; Ibn Kathir calls this route gharib, rates Saʿid b. Bashir middling, and says his report from al-Aʿmash is rare though others also transmit it.
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : كنت أصلي ، فدخل علي رجل

IBNKATHIR:107:6/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r6.claim: A second Abu Hurayra report gives the same two rewards; al-Tirmidhi calls it gharib and notes that al-Aʿmash and others also transmit the report from Habib as mursal.
IBNKATHIR:107:6/r6.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:107:5/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:5/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:5/r4.claim: Their neglect of prayer, the pillar distinguishing faith from unbelief, their ostentation, a branch of associating partners, and withholding zakāh, prayer's counterpart, expose them as deniers of judgment; even some scholars display this trait.
KASHSHAF:107:5/r4.anchor: التي هي عماد الدين ،   والفارق بين الإيمان والكفر والرياء الذي هو شعبة من الشرك

KASHSHAF:107:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:6/r1.claim: Murāʾāh is a reciprocal form of showing: the ostentatious worshipper displays his deed to people, seeking their praise and admiration.
KASHSHAF:107:6/r1.anchor: هي مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يري الناس عمله ،   وهم يرونه الثناء عليه

KASHSHAF:107:6/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:6/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:6/r2.claim: Obligatory good works should be done publicly as Islamic emblems, removing suspicion because neglecting them merits blame; voluntary acts are better concealed unless shown to encourage emulation.
KASHSHAF:107:6/r2.anchor: فمن حق الفرائض الإعلان بها وتشهيرها ،   لقوله عليه الصلاة السلام

KASHSHAF:107:6/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:6/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:6/r3.claim: Showing an act is ostentation only when the aim is to be seen and praised for piety; displaying it to encourage others is good.
KASHSHAF:107:6/r3.anchor: فإن أظهره قاصداً للاقتداء به كان جميلاً ،   وإنما الرياء أن يقصد بالإظهار أن تراه الأعين

KASHSHAF:107:6/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:6/r4.speaker: بعضهم
KASHSHAF:107:6/r4.claim: Someone saw a man prolonging a prostration of gratitude in the mosque and remarked that it would be better if done at home, suspecting ostentation and reputation-seeking.
KASHSHAF:107:6/r4.anchor: وعن بعضهم : أنه رأى رجلاً في المسجد قد سجد سجدة الشكر وأطالها

KASHSHAF:107:6/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:6/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:6/r5.claim: Avoiding ostentation is difficult except for people disciplined in sincerity.
KASHSHAF:107:6/r5.anchor: على أن اجتناب الرياء صعب إلا على المرتاضين بالإخلاص

KASHSHAF:107:6/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:6/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:107:6/r6.claim: The Prophet said ostentation is more hidden than a black ant crawling on black cloth in a dark night.
KASHSHAF:107:6/r6.anchor: الرياء أخفى من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة المظلمة على المسح الأسود

MAWARDI:107:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:6/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس
MAWARDI:107:6/r1.claim: ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas identify the hypocrites: they pray with others when seen but do not pray when alone.
MAWARDI:107:6/r1.anchor: أحدهما : المنافقون الذين يراءون بصلاتهم ، يصلونها مع الناس إذا حضروا ، ولا يصلونها إذا غابوا ، قاله علي وابن عباس .

MAWARDI:107:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:6/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:6/r2.claim: Alternatively, the warning applies generally to anyone who displays deeds without sincerely intending God's pleasure.
MAWARDI:107:6/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه عام في ذم كل من راءى بعمله ، ولم يقصد به إخلاصاً لوجه ربه .

MAWARDI:107:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:6/r3.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI:107:6/r3.claim: The Prophet reports God's saying that whoever acts for another has associated a partner with Him, while God has no need of partners.
MAWARDI:107:6/r3.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : " يقول الله تعالى : من عمل عملاً لغيري فقد أشرك بي ، وأنا أغنى الشركاء عن الشرك "

NASAFI:107:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:6/r1.claim: Nasafi connects these clauses to the preceding warning about careless prayer, framing showing off and withholding as its continuation.
NASAFI:107:6/r1.anchor: ثم وصل به قوله { فَوَيْلٌ لّلْمُصَلّينَ الذين هُمْ عَن صلاتهم سَاهُونَ

NASAFI:107:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:6/r2.claim: The warning concerns hypocrites who do not pray privately because they do not believe prayer obligatory, but pray publicly to be seen.
NASAFI:107:6/r2.anchor: يعني بهذا المنافقين لا يصلونها سراً ؛ لأنهم لا يعتقدون وجوبها ، ويصلونها علانية رياء

NASAFI:107:6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:107:6/r3.claim: An alternative says these hypocrites only outwardly join the praying, neglect prayer without seeking nearness to God or fulfilling its duty, mechanically bow and rise, display compliance, and withhold zakat and useful goods.
NASAFI:107:6/r3.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة وهم غافلون عن صلاتهم

NASAFI:107:6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:6/r6.claim: Riyā is a reciprocal form of irāʾa: the show-off displays his deed to people, who respond by showing praise and admiration.
NASAFI:107:6/r6.anchor: والمراءاة مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يرائي الناس عمله ، وهم يرونه الثناء عليه والإعجاب به

NASAFI:107:6/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:6/r7.claim: Public performance of obligatory prayers is not showing off since they should be announced; voluntary worship is better concealed, unless displayed to encourage imitation.
NASAFI:107:6/r7.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائياً بإظهار الفرائض ، فمن حقها الإعلان بها

NASAFI:107:6/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI:107:6/r8.claim: Nasafi cites the Prophet’s wording ولا غمة في فرائض الله to support openly announcing divine obligations; he states no grading.
NASAFI:107:6/r8.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  ولا غمة في فرائض الله  "

NASAFI:107:7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:7/r2.claim: The warning concerns hypocrites who do not pray privately because they do not believe prayer obligatory, but pray publicly to be seen.
NASAFI:107:7/r2.anchor: يعني بهذا المنافقين لا يصلونها سراً ؛ لأنهم لا يعتقدون وجوبها ، ويصلونها علانية رياء

NASAFI:107:7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:107:7/r3.claim: An alternative says these hypocrites only outwardly join the praying, neglect prayer without seeking nearness to God or fulfilling its duty, mechanically bow and rise, display compliance, and withhold zakat and useful goods.
NASAFI:107:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة وهم غافلون عن صلاتهم

NASAFI:107:7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:7/r6.claim: Riyā is a reciprocal form of irāʾa: the show-off displays his deed to people, who respond by showing praise and admiration.
NASAFI:107:7/r6.anchor: والمراءاة مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يرائي الناس عمله ، وهم يرونه الثناء عليه والإعجاب به

NASAFI:107:7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:7/r7.claim: Public performance of obligatory prayers is not showing off since they should be announced; voluntary worship is better concealed, unless displayed to encourage imitation.
NASAFI:107:7/r7.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائياً بإظهار الفرائض ، فمن حقها الإعلان بها

NASAFI:107:7/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI:107:7/r8.claim: Nasafi cites the Prophet’s wording ولا غمة في فرائض الله to support openly announcing divine obligations; he states no grading.
NASAFI:107:7/r8.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  ولا غمة في فرائض الله  "

QURTUBI:107:5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:5/r11.claim: Qurtubi takes the following description of people who show off as evidence that the prayer-neglecters are hypocrites.
QURTUBI:107:5/r11.anchor: ويدل على أنها في المنافقين قوله : { الذين هم يراؤون }

QURTUBI:107:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:6/r1.claim: The hypocrite presents prayer as worship while praying from fear; a sinner presents it as worship so people will say he prays.
QURTUBI:107:6/r1.anchor: الرابعة- قوله تعالى : { الذين هم يراؤون } أي يري الناس أنه يصلي طاعة وهو يصلي تقية

QURTUBI:107:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:6/r2.claim: The reality of riya is seeking worldly benefit through worship; its root motive is seeking status in people's hearts.
QURTUBI:107:6/r2.anchor: وحقيقة الرياء طلب ما في الدنيا بالعبادة

QURTUBI:107:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:107:6/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi lists four forms of riya: beautifying religious comportment (described as part of prophecy), ascetic clothing, pious-sounding speech, and displaying or beautifying worship to be seen.
QURTUBI:107:6/r3.anchor: ورابعها : الرياء بإظهار الصلاة والصدقة ، أو بتحسين الصلاة لأجل رؤية الناس ، وذلك يطول ، وهذا دليله ، قاله ابن العربي

QURTUBI:107:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:107:6/r4.claim: A Prophetic saying states that God's obligatory duties should not be concealed; Qurtubi cites it to explain public performance of the obligations.
QURTUBI:107:6/r4.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام :  " ولا غمة{[16475]} في فرائض الله "

QURTUBI:107:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:6/r5.claim: Showing obligatory worship is not riya: obligations should be public as signs of Islam and to remove suspicion about neglect; optional worship is normally better concealed, but showing it to set an example is good.
QURTUBI:107:6/r5.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائيا بإظهار العمل الصالح إن كان فريضة ، فمن حق الفرائض الإعلان بها وتشهيرها

QURTUBI:107:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:6/r6.claim: Riya occurs when someone displays worship so that onlookers will praise him for piety.
QURTUBI:107:6/r6.anchor: وإنما الرياء أن يقصد بالإظهار أن تراه الأعين ، فتثني عليه بالصلاح

QURTUBI:107:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r7.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI:107:6/r7.claim: A man saw someone prolonging a prostration of gratitude in the mosque and remarked that it would have been admirable had he done it at home, suspecting ostentation.
QURTUBI:107:6/r7.anchor: وعن بعضهم أنه رأى رجلا في المسجد قد سجد سجدة الشكر فأطالها ، فقال : ما أحسن هذا لو كان في بيتك

QURTUBI:107:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:6/r8.claim: Qurtubi points to his earlier discussion of the rule and reality of riya, including the verse on disclosing charity.
QURTUBI:107:6/r8.anchor: وقد مضى هذا المعنى في سورة " البقرة "

RAZI:107:5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r5.claim: The severe threat concerns three acts—heedlessness about prayer, showing off, and withholding al-maʿūn—raising the question why sins that do not by themselves make one an unbeliever draw such punishment.
RAZI:107:5/r5.anchor: الآية دالة على حصول التهديد العظيم بفعل ثلاثة أمور

RAZI:107:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:107:6/r1.claim: A hypocrite displays faith while hiding unbelief; a show-off displays extra humility absent from his heart to appear devout. Alternatively, the hypocrite does not pray privately, while the show-off improves his prayer before people.
RAZI:107:6/r1.anchor: أن المنافق هو المظهر للإيمان المبطن للكفر

RAZI:107:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:107:6/r2.claim: Obligatory prayer and almsgiving should be performed publicly as Islamic symbols; displaying them clears suspicion, since abandoning them merits a curse.
RAZI:107:6/r2.anchor: اعلم أنه يجب إظهار الفرائض من الصلاة والزكاة

RAZI:107:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:107:6/r3.claim: Voluntary prayers are normally concealed, unless displaying them is intended to encourage imitation.
RAZI:107:6/r3.anchor: إنما الإخفاء في النوافل إلا إذا أظهر النوافل ليقتدى به

RAZI:107:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:107:6/r4.claim: One person saw a man prolonging a prostration of gratitude in the mosque and remarked that it would have been admirable if done at home.
RAZI:107:6/r4.anchor: وعن بعضهم أنه رأى في المسجد رجلا يسجد للشكر

RAZI:107:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:107:6/r5.claim: The advice is neither to abandon voluntary prayers out of embarrassment nor to perform them for show; avoiding ostentation is rarely easy.
RAZI:107:6/r5.anchor: لا يترك النوافل حياء ولا يأتي بها رياء

RAZI:107:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r6.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI:107:6/r6.claim: The Prophet likens ostentation to something more hidden than a black ant crawling on a black surface in a dark night; no grading is stated.
RAZI:107:6/r6.anchor: الرياء أخفى من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة الظلماء

RAZI:107:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:107:6/r7.claim: The word murāʾāh is the reciprocal form of “showing”: the show-off displays his deed to people, who in turn offer praise and admiration.
RAZI:107:6/r7.anchor: هي مفاعلة من الإراءة لأن المرائي يرى الناس عمله

RAZI:107:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:107:6/r8.claim: The warning about heedlessness covers missing prayer time and inattentiveness within prayer; this verse adds ostentation, so prayer should be free of all three faults.
RAZI:107:6/r8.anchor: فظهر أن الصلاة يجب أن تكون خالية عن هذه الأحوال الثلاثة
